factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Nebius disclosed a long-term Bloom Energy partnership using behind-the-meter fuel cells to reduce dependence on new transmission build, with 328 MW planned for operation in 2026 at the first U.S. deployment.

risks: A planned 328 MW deployment is not equivalent to commissioned capacity; schedule, fuel supply, interconnection and site execution remain material.
Behind-the-meter generation reduces one grid bottleneck but does not remove GPU, construction, cooling or broader power-supply dependencies.
unknowns: This source does not establish realized utilization, uptime, delivered energy cost or return on invested capital for the fuel-cell deployment.
Alpha retains authority for factor mapping, numeric underwriting and confidence calibration.

factors.name: capacityExecution
factors.basis: The Bloom agreement supplies a concrete power-delivery mechanism and a stated 328 MW 2026 operating target, improving source-addressed visibility into how Nebius intends to convert contracted AI demand into energized capacity; completion remains unverified.

risks: Execution evidence is prospective until the planned systems are commissioned and operating at stated capacity.
unknowns: No commissioning receipt or realized operating-performance metric for the 328 MW deployment was identified in this source.

observedFacts: Nebius and Bloom Energy announced an agreement to deploy Bloom fuel-cell systems for Nebius AI infrastructure.
The systems are intended to provide behind-the-meter electricity and reduce dependence on new transmission build.
The companies stated that 328 MW of installed capacity was planned to be operational in 2026 at the first U.S. deployment.

recommendation: Alpha can use this source as direct evidence for the power-delivery/supply-chain execution path, while preserving a commissioning unknown until realized operating evidence exists.
